changelog.name: Gmoji 1.0: initial release
changelog.body:
Gmoji 1.0: initial release

Use your own color emoji font in Gboard. An Xposed-style module for Vector / LSPosed.

- Import .ttf and .ttc color emoji fonts and switch between them in one tap.
- A Gmoji row in Gboard's own settings opens a sheet with every imported font and a preview of each.
- Companion app with the same controls: import, switch, remove, reset.
- Only Gboard is affected. Other apps keep the system emoji.
- Emoji your font doesn't have fall back to the system emoji.

Requirements: Android 10+, root, Vector (or another LSPosed-compatible framework) with Gboard in scope.
Tested on: Android 17, Gboard 18.4, Vector 2.2.

Install: install the APK, enable Gmoji in Vector with Gboard in its scope, force-stop Gboard, then open Gboard settings and tap Gmoji.

readme: # Gmoji Use your own color emoji font in **Gboard**. An Xposed-style module for [Vector](https://github.com/JingMatrix/Vector) / LSPosed. - Import `.ttf` and `.ttc` color emoji fonts and switch between them in one tap. - A **Gmoji** row appears in Gboard's own settings (right under *Emojis, stickers & GIFs*) and opens a sheet with every imported font and a live preview of each. - A small companion app does the same, as a backup. - Only Gboard is affected. Other apps keep the system emoji. - Emoji your font doesn't have fall back to the system emoji, so nothing turns into an empty box. ## Requirements - Android 10 or newer, rooted - Vector (or another LSPosed-compatible framework) with module scope for Gboard - Gboard (`com.google.android.inputmethod.latin`) Developed and tested on Android 17 with Gboard 18.4 and Vector 2.2 (Zygisk Next on KernelSU). ## Install 1. Install the APK. 2. In Vector, enable **Gmoji** and make sure **Gboard** is in its scope. 3. Force-stop Gboard (or reboot) so the module loads. 4. Open Gboard settings, tap **Gmoji**, and import a font. Gboard restarts to apply it. ## Fonts Color emoji fonts in `CBDT/CBLC` (Noto style) or `COLR` format work. Other color formats are untested. For `.ttc` collections, Gmoji uses the face that contains the color glyph data. Fonts are copied into Gboard's private storage. Removing a font in Gmoji deletes that copy. ## How it works Gboard has no emoji font of its own; it draws emoji through Android's system font fallback. Inside Gboard's process only, Gmoji rebuilds the system typefaces so the chain becomes: 1. the system UI font (so digits, letters, symbols and line metrics don't change), 2. your emoji font, 3. the original system fallbacks. The font library lives in Gboard's storage (`files/gmoji/`), and the active font is a symlink at `files/gmoji.ttf` that is loaded when Gboard starts. The companion app can't read that storage, so it asks the hook running inside Gboard for the library and sends it commands (import, switch, remove, reset) by launching Gboard's settings activity with extras. Only requests whose referrer is the Gmoji app are accepted. Gboard's settings are a stock AndroidX preference screen, but its code is obfuscated. The Gmoji row is a clone of an existing row, and the members it needs are found by signature at runtime instead of by name, so it doesn't depend on obfuscated identifiers. A big Gboard update could still break it; if so, it only logs an error and the font swap keeps working. ## Build Needs a JDK and the Android SDK (build-tools and a platform). No Gradle. ```sh ./build.sh # produces build/Gmoji.apk ./build.sh install # also installs it with adb ``` The APK is signed with a throwaway key created on first build at `~/.android/gmoji-debug.jks` (override with `GMOJI_KEYSTORE`). Keep that file: updates only install over a copy signed with the same key. ## Layout ``` src/io/github/edualexxis/gmoji/ Hook.java entry point; swaps the typefaces inside Gboard Fonts.java system font families, .ttc handling, ready-made typefaces Store.java the font library inside Gboard's storage SettingsUi.java the Gmoji row, and requests from the companion app Sheet.java the bottom sheet opened by the row MainActivity.java companion app Ui.java, Previews.java shared look, and preview rendering stubs/ compile-time stubs of the Xposed API (not shipped) ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
readmeZh: # 格莫吉 在 **Gboard** 中使用您自己的彩色表情符号字体。 [Vector](https://github.com/JingMatrix/Vector) / LSPod 的 Xposed 风格模块。 - 导入“.ttf”和“.ttc”彩色表情符号字体并一键切换。 - **Gmoji** 行出现在 Gboard 自己的设置中（位于*表情符号、贴纸和 GIF* 下方），并打开一个包含每种导入字体的工作表以及每种字体的实时预览。 - 一个小型配套应用程序也可以起到同样的作用，作为备份。 - 仅 Gboard 受到影响。其他应用程序保留系统表情符号。 - 表情符号您的字体不会回退到系统表情符号，因此没有任何内容会变成空框。 ## 要求 - Android 10 或更高版本，已 root - Vector（或另一个 LSPod 兼容框架），具有 Gboard 的模块范围 - Gboard（`com.google.android.inputmethod.latin`） 在 Android 17 上使用 Gboard 18.4 和 Vector 2.2（KernelSU 上的 Zygisk Next）进行开发和测试。 ## 安装 1.安装APK。 2. 在 Vector 中，启用 **Gmoji** 并确保 **Gboard** 在其范围内。 3. 强制停止 Gboard（或重新启动）以便加载模块。 4. 打开 Gboard 设置，点击 **Gmoji**，然后导入字体。 Gboard 会重新启动以应用它。 ## 字体 “CBDT/CBLC”（Noto 风格）或“COLR”格式的彩色表情符号字体有效。其他颜色格式未经测试。对于“.ttc”集合，Gmoji 使用包含颜色字形数据的面。 字体将复制到 Gboard 的私人存储中。在 Gmoji 中删除字体会删除该副本。 ## 它是如何工作的 Gboard 没有自己的表情符号字体；它通过 Android 的系统字体后备来绘制表情符号。仅在 Gboard 的进程内，Gmoji 会重建系统字体，因此链变为： 1.系统UI字体（因此数字、字母、符号和线规格不会改变）， 2.你的表情符号字体， 3.原系统回退。 字体库位于 Gboard 的存储中 (`files/gmoji/`)，活动字体是 `files/gmoji.ttf` 处的符号链接，在 Gboard 启动时加载。配套应用程序无法读取该存储，因此它会向 Gboard 内运行的挂钩询问该库，并通过启动带有附加功能的 Gboard 设置活动来向其发送命令（导入、切换、删除、重置）。仅接受引用来源为 Gmoji 应用的请求。 Gboard 的设置是一个普通的 AndroidX 首选项屏幕，但其代码是模糊的。 Gmoji 行是现有行的克隆，它所需的成员是在运行时通过签名而不是名称找到的，因此它不依赖于混淆的标识符。 Gboard 的重大更新仍然可能会破坏它；如果是这样，它只会记录一个错误，并且字体交换继续工作。 ## 构建 需要 JDK 和 Android SDK（构建工具和平台）。没有摇篮。 ````嘘 ./build.sh # 生成 build/Gmoji.apk ./build.sh install # 也使用 adb 安装它 ```` APK 使用在第一次构建时创建的一次性密钥进行签名，该密钥位于 `~/.android/gmoji-debug.jks`（使用 `GMOJI_KEYSTORE` 覆盖）。保留该文件：更新仅安装在使用相同密钥签名的副本上。 ## 布局 ```` src/io/github/edualexxis/gmoji/ Hook.java 入口点；交换 Gboard 内的字体 Fonts.java 系统字体系列、.ttc 处理、现成字体 Store.java Gboard 存储中的字体库 SettingsUi.java Gmoji 行，以及来自配套应用程序的请求 Sheet.java 由行打开的底部工作表 MainActivity.java 配套应用程序 Ui.java、Previews.java 共享外观和预览渲染 Xpose API 的存根/编译时存根（未提供） ```` ## 许可证 [麻省理工学院]（许可证）
